diagnosis.bottleneck: The query executes two full table scans of the same table (one for each filter) and then performs a hash-based deduplication (HASH_GROUP_BY) on the combined results, causing redundant I/O and unnecessary aggregation overhead.

hypotheses.claim: UNION forces a deduplicating aggregate over both inputs. (matched: rips where trip_distance > 30 union select pulocationid, payment_type,)

The first sequential scan reads the entire table to evaluate trip_distance > 30; a single scan with a combined predicate (trip_distance > 30 OR fare_amount > 100) would eliminate the second full scan.
The second sequential scan reads the entire table again for fare_amount > 100, doubling the I/O cost; this scan is redundant if the two filters are evaluated in one pass.
